title: Backout Planner: staged quarantine windows for KV-cache and batching policy rollbacks
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a backout planning subsystem that stages config changes with quarantine windows that isolate KV-cache and batching policy impacts, using telemetry-driven thresholds to trigger safe, partial, or full rollbacks. This reduces cost-regression risk and prevents noisy global rollbacks by localizing rollback scope and providing deterministic backout steps tied to cache state and batching dynamics.

Background: Recent incidents show config flips to batching/cache policies can cause large token-cost regressions or latency spikes when applied globally. Existing automatic rollback detectors are binary and often cause broad reverts that impact availability. We need a finer-grained, state-aware mechanism that: (1) quarantines affected traffic and cached state, (2) evaluates cost/latency deltas with tunable hysteresis, (3) executes staged backouts (policy tweak, shunt traffic, snapshot restore) with a human-approvable escalation path.

Scope: Design and implement: quarantine shims for prefix/KV cache entries; a backout planner that maps telemetry signals to rollback actions; configurable windows (time + request count) and hysteresis; a dry-run simulator for candidate rollbacks; rollback playbooks for partial (shard-level), policy-level, and global reverts; integration with Console alerts and the rollouts API for canary follow-up.

Out of scope: full replacement of current change-applier agent; on-prem binary packaging (future ticket).
tasks: Design quarantine model: prefix-level and shard-level isolation
Define telemetry signals and threshold heuristics (latency p95, token-cost per-request, error-rate, KV eviction rate)
Implement backout planner service with action primitives (policy-revert, traffic-shunt, cache-snapshot-restore)
Add dry-run simulator that ingests historical telemetry and predicts rollback impact
Wire alerts and approval workflow into Redwood Console (alert -> suggested action -> approver)
Create canary policies for staged backouts (10% -> 30% -> 100%)
E2E tests: simulate config flip and assert staged rollback behavior
Docs: runbook for SEs + on-call + release notes
acceptance_criteria: Quarantine mode can isolate affected KV prefixes without affecting unrelated prefixes
Backout planner suggests a ranked list of rollback actions within 90s of anomaly detection
Staged rollback can progressively reduce scope (10%, 30%, 100%) and be paused/resumed by approver
Dry-run simulator accuracy within 20% of observed cost delta in synthetic replay tests
Console shows suggested action, ETA, and expected cost savings; approver flow triggers the action and logs audit events
No regressions on existing canary flows; performance overhead of quarantine under 3% p95 latency
comments: 2026-03-10 Asha Patel: Kicked off discovery with infra + runtime. Observed three recent incidents where global batching policy toggles spiked token cost by 2.5x. Proposal: quarantine KV prefix and run staged shunt rather than immediate global revert.

2026-03-11 Miguel Santos: Spike analysis attached (link). Proposing action primitives: 'policy-toggle', 'traffic-redirect', 'cache-restore-snapshot'. Need API changes to allow transient policy overrides at routing layer.
2026-03-11 Elena Kwan: Design review — prioritize simple, auditable actions first. Recommend adding an opt-in 'sim-only' mode for first rollout to validate planner suggestions.

2026-03-12 Miguel Santos: Implemented initial simulator scaffolding and prefix quarantine prototype. Early results: quarantine reduces blast radius in our synthetic load tests; dry-run predictions skew low on token-cost for short-lived workloads — tuning thresholds required.
2026-03-12 Asha Patel: Follow-up: add telemetry counter for KV eviction rate and batch-size distribution. We should include cost-per-request as a normalized metric across models.
